newsitem.title: JAPAN: DOLLAR SEEN CAPPED, FOCUS ON TRADE ISSUE.
newsitem.headline: DOLLAR SEEN CAPPED, FOCUS ON TRADE ISSUE.

text.p: The dollar is expected to be capped against the yen in Asia on Thursday following its overnight falls as U.S.-Japanese trade tensions grew on comments by U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky, dealers said.
"We thought that the market was buying dollars (against the yen) on economic fundamentals, but the focus is shifting back to the trade issue again," a city bank dealer said.
"I expect the upside of the dollar to be capped after the overnight dips on Barshefsky's comments," the dealer said.
Dealers said offers were lined up around 119.20 yen with firm resistance around 119.50 yen.
Barshefsky told reporters in Washington that U.S. officials were concerned that car exports to Japan had decreased and the trade deficit with Japan in general was deteriorating.
"Obviously we are concerned that Japan not export its way out of its current economic situation," she said.
On Wednesday in Tokyo, comments by a U.S. official helped depress the dollar against the yen.

Lawrence Greenwood, economic minister-counsellor at the U.S. embassy in Tokyo, said in an interview with Reuters that rises in Japan's current account surplus have the potential to create an explosive situation with the United States.
But dealers said concerns about trade tension should not be a factor causing the dollar to be heavily sold against the yen.
They said Japanese institutional investors were still eager to buy dollars, with buying orders spotted around 118.30 yen. Japanese importers were also expected to buy below 118 yen.
"The dollar's basic undertone remains strong, so many operators are unwilling to build up fresh short positions aggressively now," another dealer said.
Dealers expect the dollar/mark to travel in a boxed range of around 1.8750 to 1.8850 marks in Asia.
Dealers said they will be watching the mark/yen closely as the mark selling pressure remains strong due to lingering bearishness of the German currency.
"We have to watch out for the mark/yen. Sharp falls in the mark/yen could become a key factor to drag down the dollar/yen," the first dealer said.
At 2326 GMT, the mark fell to 62.85/88 yen, compared with 63.06 yen in New York on Wednesday.
